column4: In this chapter we will study the authority and power of Christ, which authorities and powers He has delegated to us (His church), and how to operate in the authority of the name of Jesus. We will also study angelic and demonic beings and examine their authority, power, and natures.
column5: In this chapter we will study the authority and power of Christ, the authority and power He has delegated to us (His church), and how to operate in the authority given in Jesus’ name. We will also study angelic and demonic beings and examine their authority, power, and nature.

column4: Authority means having the right to act. Power is the ability to carry it out. Both are essential in the spiritual life. Authority is different from power. Let’s look at the following table which compares authority & power and consider a few examples.

column4: Here are a few examples to help understand the difference between power and authority.
column5: Here are a few examples to illustrate the difference between power and authority.

column4: Example 1: At work, an employee may have the talents and skills to conduct a sale of the company's assets (power). This power is lawful if they also have the associated permission (authority) from the company’s owners. Without this authority, selling the company's assets is theft.
column5: Example 1: In the workplace, an employee may have the talent and skill (power) to sell the company’s assets. This power is legitimate if they also have the relevant authorization (authority) from the owners of the company. Selling the company’s assets without this authority is theft.

column4: Example 2: A police officer is given special training in weapons and hand-to-hand combat to learn how to apprehend and physically compel a criminal (power). Police officers have been given the job responsibility backed up by laws (authority) to enforce criminal statutes.
column5: Example 2: A police officer is given special training in weapons and hand-to-hand combat to learn how to arrest and physically subdue an offender (power). Police officers are given a legally sanctioned job responsibility (authority) to enforce criminal statutes.

column4: ## The Source of Jesus’ Authority
column5: ## The source of Jesus' authority

column4: Now that we have looked at precisely what authority is we need to know who the source of that authority is. Jesus’ authority is both divine and delegated. It originates from God the Father, is affirmed through His death and resurrection, and operates in perfect harmony with the Father’s will. Though absolute, His authority respects human free will, demonstrating God’s love rather than forceful control.
column5: Now that we have seen exactly what authority is, we must know who the source of that authority is। Jesus’ authority is both divine and delegated। It originates from God the Father, is confirmed through His death and resurrection, and operates in perfect harmony with the Father’s will। Though absolute, His authority respects human free will, displaying God’s love rather than coercive control।

column4: Jesus’ authority is rooted in His divine identity as the Son of God and is granted by the Father. The Father entrusted all authority to Christ, including judgment and rule over heaven and earth (Matthew 11:27). Jesus’ authority reflects the unity and love within the Trinity, where the Son carries out the Father’s plan perfectly (John 3:35).
column5: Jesus’ authority is rooted in His divine identity as the Son of God, and it is granted by the Father। The Father has entrusted to Christ all authority, including judgment and rule over heaven and earth (Matthew 11:27)। Jesus’ authority reflects the unity and love within the Trinity, wherein the Son perfectly accomplishes the Father’s plan (John 3:35)।

column4: While Jesus had inherent authority as God’s Son, His victory over sin, death, and hell was fully established through His death and resurrection. Christ’s obedience in His sacrifice led to His exaltation (seated at the right hand of the Father), securing His authority over all creation. By conquering death, Christ gained absolute dominion over life and eternity.
column5: Although Jesus had inherent authority as the Son of God, His victory over sin, death, and hell was fully established through His death and resurrection। Christ’s obedience in self-sacrifice exalted Him in glory (seated at the right hand of the Father), solidifying His authority over all creation। By conquering death, Christ obtained supreme dominion over life and eternity।

column4: ## Jesus Delegated Certain Authority to His Followers
column5: ## Jesus has delegated specific authority to His followers

column4: Jesus delegated specific areas of authority to believers. This authority is relational. We only have this authority in relationship to Jesus. We have no authority apart from our relationship with Jesus. Likewise, the power we have been given by the Holy Spirit is only through our relationship with Him. Apart from Him, we can do nothing.

column4: ## Laying on of Hands
column5: ## Laying on of hands

column4: The laying on of hands is a significant biblical practice used throughout both the Old Testament and New Testament to symbolize blessing, commissioning, healing, and the impartation of spiritual authority or gifts. It is more than just a physical act-it represents a spiritual connection and transfer under the direction of God’s authority.
column5: The laying on of hands is an important biblical practice used throughout both the Old and New Testaments to symbolize blessing, commissioning, healing, and the impartation of spiritual authority or gifts. It is not merely a physical action—it represents a spiritual connection and transfer under the direction of God's authority.

column4: In the Old Testament, the laying on of hands was often associated with blessing and dedication. For example, Jacob blessed his grandchildren, Ephraim, and Manasseh, by laying his hands on them (Genesis 48:14). Similarly, Moses laid hands on Joshua to commission him as his successor, imparting leadership authority and wisdom (Numbers 27:18-23, Deuteronomy 34:9). This act publicly signified God’s selection and empowerment for the task ahead.
column5: In the Old Testament, the laying on of hands was often associated with blessing and consecration. For example, Jacob laid his hands on his grandsons, Ephraim and Manasseh, and blessed them (Genesis 48:14). Likewise, Moses laid his hands on Joshua, appointing him as his successor and imparting leadership authority and wisdom (Numbers 27:18-23, Deuteronomy 34:9). This act was a public acknowledgment of God's choice and empowerment for the task ahead.

column4: In the New Testament, the laying on of hands is closely tied to the ministry of Jesus and the early church. Jesus regularly laid hands on the sick to heal them (Mark 6:5, Luke 4:40), demonstrating both compassion and authority over sickness and disease. The apostles continued this practice, using it to impart the Holy Spirit (Acts 8:17), spiritual gifts (1 Timothy 4:14, 2 Timothy 1:6), and blessings to believers. It also played a role in commissioning leaders and missionaries for ministry (Acts 13:3).

It also played a role in appointing leaders and missionaries to ministry (Acts 13:3).

column4: The laying on of hands symbolizes an act of faith and obedience to God’s Word. It is not a mechanical ritual, but a spiritual practice rooted in dependence on the Holy Spirit. For example, in Acts 6:6, the apostles laid hands on those selected to serve as deacons, committing them to God’s service and publicly acknowledging their calling. In Acts 19:6, Paul laid hands on believers, and they received the Holy Spirit, demonstrating its role in spiritual empowerment.

column4: ### Angels
column5: ### Angels

column4: Angels are a significant part of God’s creation, serving as His messengers and agents to carry out His divine purposes. The Bible reveals a spiritual realm inhabited by these beings, who are powerful, intelligent, and obedient to God’s commands. While angels are often unseen, their presence and actions impact human history and spiritual warfare. Understanding their roles, classifications, and activities provides us with deeper insight into God’s plan and the unseen realities that surround us.
column5: Angels are an important part of God's creation; they carry out His divine purposes as His messengers and representatives. The Bible reveals a spiritual realm where these beings dwell—who are powerful, intelligent, and obedient to God's commands. Although angels are often unseen, their presence and activities influence human history and spiritual warfare. Understanding their roles, classifications, and functions gives us deeper insight into God's plan and the unseen realities around us.

column4: The term "angel" itself means "messenger," highlighting their primary function. Angels operate in obedience to God’s will, whether delivering messages, providing protection, executing judgment, or engaging in spiritual battles. They are not objects of worship but serve as examples of obedience and reverence, always pointing back to the glory of God. This chapter explores the nature, classifications, and roles of angels, shedding light on their significance in Scripture and in our lives today.
column5: The word "angel" itself means "messenger," which points to their primary task. Angels work in obedience to God's will—whether delivering messages, providing protection, executing judgment, or engaging in spiritual warfare. They are not objects of worship; rather, they are examples of obedience and devotion who always direct attention to the glory of God. This chapter discusses the nature, classifications, and roles of angels, clarifying their significance in Scripture and in our lives today.

column4: In the scriptures angels are seen as **messengers**, **servants**, and **warriors**. Angels frequently act as messengers, delivering important announcements, warnings, and encouragements. They reveal God’s plans and provide guidance in times of need (Luke 1:26-38; Matthew 2:13; Revelation 1:1). Angels are actively involved in protecting, strengthening, and delivering believers. They minister to God’s people in times of distress and provide supernatural aid (Psalms 91:11; Acts 12:7-11; Matthew 4:11). Angels engage in spiritual warfare, battling demonic forces to advance God’s kingdom and defend believers (Daniel 10:13; Revelation 12:7-9).

They minister to God's people in times of trouble and provide miraculous assistance (Psalm 91:11; Acts 12:7-11; Matthew 4:11). Angels engage in spiritual warfare, contending against demonic forces to advance God's kingdom and protect believers (Daniel 10:13; Revelation 12:7-9).

column4: #### The Nature of Angels
column5: #### The Nature of Angels

column4: Angels are created beings, brought into existence by God before the foundation of the world. They are distinct from humans, possessing unique characteristics that equip them for their heavenly roles. The Bible teaches that angels are spiritual beings, not bound by physical limitations, yet they can take on visible forms when interacting with humans.

They are distinct from humans, possessing unique characteristics that make them suited to their heavenly roles. The Bible teaches that angels are spiritual beings—not bound by physical limitations; yet in interactions with humans they can take on visible form.

column4: Angels are described as immortal, meaning they do not die or age. They are innumerable, with vast hosts filling the heavenly realms. While they are often referred to with masculine pronouns, Scripture makes it clear that angels are sexless and do not marry or reproduce. These qualities emphasize their purpose as servants of God, entirely devoted to His will and commands. Angels possess remarkable traits that reflect their divine purpose. They are obedient, reverent, wise, and powerful. These qualities equip them to carry out God’s will effectively and faithfully.

column5: #### The Origin and Nature of Evil Spirits

column4: Demons are fallen angels who followed Satan’s rebellion against God. *(Revelation 12:7-9; Matthew 25:41).* Satan, formerly known as Lucifer (“light bearer”), an exalted angel, sought to exalt himself above God and was cast out of heaven along with other rebellious angels. *(Isaiah 14:12-15; Ezekiel 28:12-17).*
column5: Evil spirits are those fallen angels who joined Satan in his rebellion against God. *(Revelation 12:7-9; Matthew 25:41).* Satan, formerly known as Lucifer (“light-bearer”), was a high-ranking angel who sought to exalt himself above God and was cast out of heaven along with the other rebellious angels. *(Isaiah 14:12-15; Ezekiel 28:12-17).*

column4: Demons are spirits without physical bodies but can oppress and torment humans and animals. *(Mark 5:11-13).* They seek to deceive, tempt, oppress, and destroy. *(John 10:10; 2 Corinthians 11:14). Unlike God,* they have limits, and are not omnipresent (everywhere), omniscient (all knowing), omnipotent (all powerful)*.* Their ultimate defeat is certain, and they will face eternal punishment. *(Revelation 20:10)*

column4: The gospels and epistles further clarify the work of the enemy. Evil spirits, as disembodied, largely must do their work through willing and open vessels. God works through people, so does the devil. This oppression is often marked by torment, self-harm, and destructive behaviors *(Luke 8:27-29).* Their attacks cause fear, temptation, and discouragement *(2 Corinthians 12:7).* The most common source of their power (not authority) in someone's life is through the influence of lies and emotional strongholds *(2 Corinthians 10:3-5).*
column5: The Gospels and the Epistles make the enemy’s work even clearer. Evil spirits, being disembodied, often are forced to accomplish their work through willing and open persons. Just as God works through people, so does Satan. This oppression often manifests through torment, self-harm, and destructive behavior *(Luke 8:27-29).* Their attacks produce fear, temptation, and discouragement *(2 Corinthians 12:7).* The most common source of their power (not authority) in a person’s life is the influence of lies and emotional strongholds *(2 Corinthians 10:3-5).*

column4: It's important to note that not every lie a person believes, infirmity in their body, or stronghold in their life is the direct result of demonic influence, but these places of woundedness are places where the enemy can exploit us and keep us in a place of frustration and oppression.

column4: To deal with an evil or unclean spirit the pattern expressed in the scriptures is to take authority over it in the name of Jesus and command it to leave. The Holy Spirit promises to give us wisdom and discernment if we ask! (James 1:5). We don’t need to make it a production, or a drama like in the movies, or to even talk with them, that is a trick of the devil to distract us. Satan's power is established and maintained only by the lies He can get us to believe.

column4: There are two major cautions in the scriptures when dealing with the demonic:
column5: There are two major cautions in Scripture when dealing with demonic matters:

column4: 1. **Only those with a relationship with Jesus have the authority over the demonic**. Acts 19:11-20 talks about sons of a Jewish Chief Priest named Sceva. They tried to intervene in the life of someone who was oppressed and tormented by the devil and the evil spirit refused to leave because they didn’t have a relationship with Jesus. The man who was oppressed leapt on them, stripped them naked and beat them. Just as you should not impersonate a police officer, **don't impersonate someone with a relationship with Jesus, instead have a relationship with Jesus**!
column5: 1. **Only those who have a relationship with Jesus have authority over demonic power**. Acts 19:11-20 tells of the sons of a Jewish chief priest named Sceva. They tried to intervene in the life of a man who was oppressed and tormented by the devil, and because they had no relationship with Jesus, the evil spirit refused to come out. The man who was oppressed leapt on them, stripped them naked, and beat them. Just as you should not pretend to be a police officer, **do not pretend to be someone who has a relationship with Jesus; rather, build a relationship with Jesus**!

column4: 2. **When an evil spirit leaves, it goes away for a time and will try to come back**. If it finds the place it had dwelled empty, it will come back worse. Matthew 12:43-45. When we minister to a person oppressed of the devil, that person needs to fill the void that evil spirit occupied in their lives. That means at a minimum establishing a personal relationship with Jesus and strengthening it by obedience to the Holy Spirit. Often an evil or unclean spirit has power to operate in someone’s life through the choices they made, based on their beliefs. Anyone delivered from the devil needs to replace that old belief system and be transformed by the renewal of their minds (Romans 12:1-2).
column5: 2. **When an evil spirit leaves, it stays away for a time and tries to return**. If it finds the place where it lived empty, it returns in an even worse way. Matthew 12:43-45. When we minister to someone oppressed by the devil, that person must fill the void in their life that the evil spirit occupied. This means at the very least establishing a personal relationship with Jesus and strengthening that relationship by obeying the Holy Spirit. Often a wicked or unclean spirit gains the ability to operate in someone’s life through decisions they make based on their beliefs. Anyone who has been delivered from the devil must be transformed by the renewing of their mind, replacing that old belief system (Romans 12:1-2).

column4: We serve an awesome and mighty God, and we are ‘more than conquerors’ (Romans 8:37) over the defeated enemy. We have no need to fear our defeated enemy, for Jesus has given us His authority to crush his head! The devil’s time is short, and He will ultimately be judged along with every principality and power on the earth that rejects the dominion of Christ.
